# Infantry AI

> Infantry AI is a command post for coding agents: a daemon with a ticket board, agents on their own git branches, mail, shared project knowledge, Lua scripts and hooks, plus a desktop app (Tauri 2 with a React front end), an Android app and the `infantry` CLI. The main branch is the Rust framework: the daemon is a Rust binary, every feature is a plugin (a module with a `module.json` and a WASM or sidecar daemon half). Core is MPL-2.0, everything else Apache-2.0.

Read AGENTS.md first. Facts in these docs come from the code; where an older design record disagrees, the code wins. The Kotlin version is on the `legacy-java` branch.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the guide for AI coding agents: rules, repo layout, build and test commands, where each change goes.
- [Architecture](docs/wiki/Architecture.md): the daemon, the layers, the wire, plugins, a request from the app to the daemon and back, scripting.
- [Install](docs/wiki/Install.md): the Windows installer, the headless daemon, `infantry` on PATH, building from source.
- [Android](docs/wiki/Android.md): the Android app, pairing a phone to a daemon, building the APK.
- [Updates](docs/wiki/Updates.md): the stable and nightly channels, the feed, signing, the release pipeline.
- [Command line](docs/wiki/CommandLine.md): the native `infantry` command.
- [Recipes](docs/wiki/recipes/README.md): worked "how to add X" guides with the files to touch.

## Build plugins

- [Plugins](docs/wiki/Plugins.md): `module.json`, the daemon half (WASM component or sidecar), grants, the official plugins, building with `rust/plugins/stage.sh`.
- [Make a plugin](docs/wiki/make-a-plugin.md): from an official plugin to a built daemon half.
- [Web UI plugins](docs/wiki/Web-UI-plugins.md): a plugin's web UI half: the `ui` manifest block, the slots, `@infantry/ui-plugin-api`, scoped styles, faults, the trust model and the Tauri CSP.
- [Daemon plugin API](docs/wiki/daemon-plugin-api.md): the WIT world: exports, imports, frames, tools, routes, hooks, events.
- [Plugin knowledge](docs/wiki/plugin-knowledge.md): module.json `knowledge` and the PLUGIN TOOLS briefing.
- [Plugin lifecycle](docs/wiki/Plugin-lifecycle.md): install, update, enable, disable, remove.
- [Publish a plugin](docs/wiki/publish-a-plugin.md): package a plugin from its own repo.

## Run and automate

- [Harnesses](docs/wiki/Harnesses.md): the harness contract and the four harness crates (Claude Code, Codex, opencode, pi).
- [Runners](docs/wiki/runner-quickstart.md): local and linked remote runners, setup, troubleshooting.
- [Scripting](docs/wiki/Scripting.md): the sandboxed Lua API, hooks, the process bridge.
- [Settings](docs/wiki/Settings.md): scopes (app, project, role, session) and cost-saving defaults.
- [Health](docs/wiki/Health.md): the daemon health and environment report.
- [Notifications](docs/wiki/Notifications.md): the notification bus and its presenters.
- [Board](docs/wiki/Board.md): tickets, lanes and epics.
- [Secrets](docs/wiki/Secrets.md) and [Vault](docs/wiki/Vault.md): saved secrets and the encrypted vault.
